name: HivePunk 632
subject: Uniswap v4 hooks and hook-validation tools
thesis: Hooks make v4 pools programmable and have attracted large-scale research and aggregator flow, but the same pages show trust infrastructure lags permissionless deployment, so validation quality remains the deciding unknown.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Uniswap v4 hooks are specially designed contracts that run at distinct points throughout a pool action's lifecycle and serve as plugins to tailor how pools, swaps, fees, and LP positions interact.
claims.quote: Uniswap v4 Hooks -- also known simply as hooks -- are specially designed contracts that run at distinct points throughout a pool action's lifecycle. They serve as plugins allowing developers to tailor how pools, swaps, fees, and LP positions interact.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: A hook invokes custom logic at four critical phases: Initialize, Modify Position, Swap, and Donate, with before/after callbacks for each.
claims.quote: 🔄 Lifecycle During the course of a pool action's lifecycle, a hook invokes custom logic primarily at four critical phases: Initialize : Activated when the pool is deployed.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Once a pool is initialized with a specific hook, it cannot be changed, removed, or swapped.
claims.quote: That hook is immutable: once a pool is initialized with a specific hook, it cannot be changed, removed, or swapped.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: There is a Uniswap Hook Official Allowlist described as a per-chain allowlist of hook contract addresses that Uniswap routing API is permitted to route trades through.
claims.quote: Uniswap Hook Official Allowlist : A per-chain allowlist of Uniswap V4 hook contract addresses that Uniswap routing API is permitted to route trades through.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: 0x's research into more than 84,000 Uniswap v4 hooks exposed a challenge that production liquidity needs a trust layer.
claims.quote: 0x’s research into more than 84,000 Uniswap v4 hooks exposed a major challenge for modular AMMs: extensibility is powerful, but production liquidity needs a trust layer.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: A single misconfigured or malicious Hook can lead to significant financial losses, denial-of-service conditions, or manipulation of the pool.
claims.quote: A single misconfigured or malicious Hook can lead to significant financial losses, denial-of-service conditions, or manipulation of the pool.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Anyone can create a pool, the creator chooses which Hook if any to use, and once a pool is created you cannot change the Hook.
claims.quote: Crucially, once a pool is created, you cannot change the Hook.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Uniswap v4 was reported as $1.197B TVL, $131.4M in 30d fees, and $42.34B in 30d volume.
claims.quote: Uniswap v4 : $1.197B TVL, $131.4M in 30d fees, $42.34B in 30d volume — annualized fees/TVL of 131.7% , ~3.2x its own non-hooked predecessor Uniswap V3 (41.2%) .

claims.label: FACT

claims.label: DERIVED
claims.text: Because hooks are immutable at pool creation and creators choose them permissionlessly, every pool permanently inherits its chosen hook's risk profile.
claims.math: c3 (immutable/no change) + c7 (creator chooses hook, many pools per pair) => permanent per-pool hook risk

risks: A single misconfigured or malicious hook can lead to significant financial losses, denial-of-service conditions, or manipulation of the pool.
Permissionless hooks mean anyone can create a pool and choose any hook, with many pools for the same pair using different hooks.
Hook reentrancy traps, asymmetric gas costs and pool-specific simulation break universal V2/V3 arb bots.
Custom curves and dynamic fees can be mispriced by generic bots assuming static tiers.
Curated-list activity may be stale, limiting its use as a live validator.
